theme.en: Seventy-seven kilometres to the first temple

narrative.en: Tosa's first temple stands 77.5 km from the section's first step, and this day walks 32.1 of them. Nothing on it carries a temple number. What the record holds instead is a railway — six stations, Hiwasa in the first half-kilometre, then Yamagawachi, Hegawa, Mugi, Sabase and Kaifu at 28.8 km — and, at 8.6 km, a ruined restaurant. No temple falls 25 to 30 km ahead of the section's start, so the day ends at a bed rather than a gate: the Haryugetu Guesthouse, 32.1 km on.

reflection.en: Hotsumisaki-ji is still 45.5 km ahead when this day ends — what does a day hold when nothing on it is a gate?

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/10810952434 (accommodation), 62.89 km along this section's walked line, 14 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 32.08 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 30.81 km on.

theme.en: Twenty-four bus stops, and still no temple

narrative.en: A second day, 30.8 km, and the section's first temple is still 14.7 km beyond where it ends. Twenty-four of the thirty-seven places recorded here are bus stops. Three sacred places break that run early — Kumano Shrine and Myōken-gū inside the first 7 km, Meitokuji at 44.0 km — and then nothing at all is marked for 9.4 km, the longest unrecorded stretch of the day. It ends where the day before it ended, at a bed: Tokumasu Minshuku, 62.9 km into the section.

reflection.en: Two days, 62.9 km, and no temple yet — what are you walking toward while the thing you are walking toward has not appeared?

end.note: Temple 26, 88.08 km along this section's walked line, 5 m off it — 25.19 km from the previous day's end at 62.89 km, inside the 25-30 km band and, of the temples in it, the one nearest 27.5 km.

theme.en: The first temple, and then two more

narrative.en: Two days and 62.9 km have passed with no temple on them; this day reaches the first 14.7 km in. Hotsumisaki-ji, then Shinshō-ji 6.7 km on, then Kongōchō-ji 3.8 km after that — the shortest step between any two temples in Tosa, and the day ends at its gate. Sixty-one places stand on this day, more than on any other in the section, and forty-four of them are bus stops. Three temples inside 10.5 km, after seventy-seven and a half kilometres with none.

reflection.en: Seventy-seven kilometres for the first gate and ten and a half for the next two — which of those two rhythms is the pilgrimage?

end.note: Temple 27, 116.63 km along this section's walked line, 53 m off it — 28.55 km from the previous day's end at 88.08 km, inside the 25-30 km band and, of the temples in it, the one nearest 27.5 km.

narrative.en: Kongōchō-ji to Kōnomine-ji is 28.5 km, and it is the only one of Tosa's sixteen temple-to-temple legs that falls inside the 25 to 30 km band the day cut looks in. So this day is a leg exactly: one gate to the next, with nothing for the rule to choose between. Nahari comes 18.9 km in, the first town the section records. Fifty-six places stand on the day and forty of them are bus stops, and two more waypoints sit within 15 m of Kōnomine-ji itself — a shrine, and a second entry carrying the temple's own name.

reflection.en: The one day here that is also a single leg between two gates — does knowing that change how you walk it?

name.en: Konomine-ji (Temple 27) to 黒潮温泉ホテル

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/1762646861 (accommodation), 152.39 km along this section's walked line, 57 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 116.63 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 35.76 km on.

narrative.en: Kōnomine-ji to Dainichi-ji is 38.4 km and this day takes 35.8 of it, so no temple stands on it at all. What the record holds changes character: eleven railway stations, twelve public toilets and ten convenience stores, against the bus stops that carried the three days before — two bus stops here, against forty on the day before. The city of Aki comes at 130.2 km and a viewpoint at 137.6. The day ends at a hotel at 152.4 km, 2.6 km short of the temple it has been walking toward.

reflection.en: Two temples thirty-eight kilometres apart, and neither of them on this day — what is a day worth that is only the space between?

name.en: 黒潮温泉ホテル to Chikurin-ji (Temple 31)

end.note: Temple 31, 177.82 km along this section's walked line, 72 m off it — 25.43 km from the previous day's end at 152.39 km, inside the 25-30 km band and, of the temples in it, the one nearest 27.5 km.

narrative.en: After 38.4 km with none, four temples fall inside this one day. Dainichi-ji stands 2.6 km in, Tosa Kokubun-ji 9.2 km after it, Zenraku-ji 7.1 km after that, and Chikurin-ji 6.5 km further, closing the day at 177.8 km — 22.8 km from the first of them to the last. The city of Konan stands at 153.3 km, inside the day's first kilometre, and five convenience stores stand on the day. Twenty-six places in all, four of them temples.

reflection.en: Four gates in twenty-three kilometres after thirty-eight with none — how quickly can attention change its pace?

theme.en: Four hundred and fifty-seven metres out of the band

narrative.en: Three temples come early — Zenjibu-ji 6.1 km in, Sekkei-ji 8.2 km after it, Tanema-ji 6.3 km after that — and then the day has to find somewhere to stop. Kiyotaki-ji, the next one, stands 30.5 km from where this day began: 457 m past the 30 km edge of the band the cut ends days in. So the day ends at Tosa instead, the city, at 205.3 km. Twenty places are recorded on it, four of them shrines and four of them hospitals.

reflection.en: Four hundred and fifty-seven metres decided where this day ends. How much of any day is decided that finely?

name.en: Tosa to Ohenro Guest House Lilian

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/11372865970 (accommodation), 226.42 km along this section's walked line, 18 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 205.29 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 21.14 km on.

theme.en: Two gates, and almost nothing between them

narrative.en: Kiyotaki-ji stands 3.0 km into the day and Shōryū-ji 14.5 km beyond it, and between them one thing reaches the day: Shōnen-ji, 10.3 km after the first gate. Seven places reach it in all, the fewest so far in Tosa. Past Shōryū-ji the next temple is 58.1 km away, and no temple falls where a day beginning here would end, so it stops at the Ohenro Guest House Lilian — 21.1 km, the shortest day the section has cut so far.

reflection.en: Twenty-one kilometres, two gates, and one marked thing between them — what fills a day the record leaves blank?

name.en: Ohenro Guest House Lilian to 民宿あわの里

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/12898846612 (accommodation), 252.98 km along this section's walked line, 207 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 226.42 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 26.56 km on.

theme.en: Nineteen kilometres before anything is marked

narrative.en: This day walks 19.4 km before the record marks a single place — the longest such opening anywhere in Tosa. What comes after comes quickly: two convenience stores, the city of Susaki at 247.6 km, a station, a toilet, and the day's end at 253.0 km. Six places on 26.6 km, the fewest of any day here so far, and no temple on it: the next stands 54.5 km beyond where this one began.

reflection.en: Nineteen kilometres and nothing on the map to mark them — is that an absence, or a kind of quiet?

name.en: 民宿あわの里 to Iwamoto-ji (Temple 37)

end.note: Temple 37, 280.88 km along this section's walked line, 21 m off it — 27.90 km from the previous day's end at 252.98 km, inside the 25-30 km band and, of the temples in it, the one nearest 27.5 km.

theme.en: The last six hundred metres hold the day

narrative.en: Iwamoto-ji closes this day at 280.9 km, 58.1 km on from Shōryū-ji — the third-widest gap between temples in Tosa — and the day walks the last 27.9 of it. For most of that the record runs thin and strung along a railway: six stations, five places to eat. Then the last 0.6 km takes six of the day's twenty-one places at once — two Kubokawa stations, the town of Shimanto, two places to stay, a toilet — and the temple after them.

reflection.en: Fifty-eight kilometres between two gates, and most of what the day holds arrives in its last six hundred metres. What does nearness do to distance?

theme.en: The first of three days in one gap

narrative.en: Iwamoto-ji to Kongōfuku-ji is 82.7 km, the widest gap between two temples in this section, and the cut spends three whole days and the first 59 m of a fourth crossing it. This is the first of the three, 28.2 km. Nineteen places stand on it — five railway stations, three shrines, three places to eat — and at 303.2 km the only water source recorded anywhere in Tosa, a fountain. It ends at a henro house at 309.0 km, with 54.5 km of the gap still ahead.

reflection.en: Eighty-three kilometres between one gate and the next, and this day covers a third of it — how do you hold a distance you cannot finish?

name.en: Henro House Maaru to 民宿いさりび

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/12908978212 (accommodation), 342.61 km along this section's walked line, 13 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 309.05 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 33.56 km on.

narrative.en: The middle day of the 82.7 km gap, and the longest of the three at 33.6 km. Thirteen places reach it. Four railway stations come in the first 7.4 km, then a viewpoint and the town of Kuroshio at 318.4 km — and after that the record almost stops: 7.3 km with nothing marked, a convenience store, a café and two toilets, then 7.5 km more with nothing marked before the day ends at a minshuku at 342.6 km. No temple has stood on the line for 61.7 km.

reflection.en: Sixty-two kilometres since the last gate and twenty-one still to the next — what keeps a day like this from being only transit?

name.en: 民宿いさりび to 金剛福寺宿坊

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/9444928782 (accommodation), 363.53 km along this section's walked line, 145 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 342.61 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 20.92 km on.

theme.en: Fifty-nine metres short of a gate

narrative.en: Five places to stay stand in the first 3.4 km of this day, the tightest run of beds anywhere in Tosa; then it goes 17.6 km to its end. Kongōfuku-ji is 21.0 km from where the day began — too near for the 25 to 30 km band the cut ends days in — so no temple qualified, and the day stops 59 m short of the gate, at a lodging that carries the temple's own name. In the last 200 m before it the record gathers two viewpoints, two toilets and a bus stop named Cape Ashizuri.

reflection.en: Fifty-nine metres from the gate, and the day ends anyway, because the rule measured from somewhere else. Is arriving a place, or a decision?

name.en: 金剛福寺宿坊 to Ocean, River, Mountain Retreat

end.note: OpenStreetMap node/11535055771 (accommodation), 399.33 km along this section's walked line, 24 m off it. No temple falls 25-30 km past the previous day's end at 363.53 km, so the day ends at the named accommodation or town waypoint on the line nearest 27.5 km, 35.80 km on.

theme.en: One gate, then thirty-six kilometres unmarked

narrative.en: Kongōfuku-ji stands 59 m into this day, and past it the record holds nothing for 35.7 km — the longest stretch in Tosa with nothing marked on it. Six places are filed on the day and three of them are lodgings 0.9 to 1.5 km off the walked line, which this day never reaches; what is left is the temple, the lodging the day starts from, and the place it ends. Kongōfuku-ji to Enkō-ji is 54.9 km, and this day takes 35.8 of them, all of it past the gate.

reflection.en: Thirty-six kilometres with nothing on the map to mark them — what do you notice when nothing is pointed out to you?

name.en: Ocean, River, Mountain Retreat to Enkō-ji (Temple 39)

theme.en: The shortest day, and the last gate

narrative.en: 19.2 km, the shortest day in Tosa, and it ends at Enkō-ji — the section's own boundary, where Iyo begins from the same point. Nine places stand on it: a guest house at 402.1 km, then Mihara at 406.7, the only village among the section's eight towns, Yamabiko Cafe just past it, two toilets, a station at 415.9, a restaurant, and a hospital inside the last kilometre. Kongōfuku-ji to Enkō-ji is 54.9 km, and this day is its last 19.2.

reflection.en: Fifteen days, 418.5 km, sixteen gates — and the last of them is the next section's first. What do you set down here?
